entries.6ffe98bc081380ca: YAMAHA CORPORATION, together with 61 subsidiaries and 5 affiliates, makes up the group. Its head office is at 10-1 Nakazawa-cho, Naka-ku, Hamamatsu City, and consolidated employees number 17,886 (as of March 31, 2026; temporary employees, shown as external figures, number 5,730). Roles are divided: pianos are made at the Kakegawa Plant (Kakegawa City, Shizuoka Prefecture, and elsewhere), electronic instruments, orchestral and percussion instruments, and professional sound equipment are made at the Toyooka Plant (Iwata City, Shizuoka Prefecture, and elsewhere), and automotive interior components and FA equipment are made at the Tenryu Plant (Naka-ku, Hamamatsu City). There are also manufacturing subsidiaries in China (Tianjin, Hangzhou and Suzhou), Indonesia and Malaysia. For sales, YAMAHA MUSIC JAPAN CO., LTD. handles Japan, and overseas sales are handled by Yamaha Corporation of America in the United States, Yamaha Music Europe GmbH in Germany, and others. This company is separate from [[company:yamaha-motor|Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd.]], which was formed in 1955 when its motorcycle division was spun off. The two companies share the common "Yamaha" brand. As of March 31, 2026, YAMAHA CORPORATION held 28,928,370 shares of Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. (carrying amount of ¥32,558 million), and Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. is the sixth-largest shareholder of YAMAHA CORPORATION, holding 3.20% of its issued shares (excluding treasury shares). However, Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. does not appear in the status of affiliated companies (the tables of consolidated subsidiaries and affiliates accounted for under the equity method).

entries.8a863d51fc68dd77: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥465,330 million, an increase of ¥3,250 million (0.7%) from ¥462,080 million in the previous fiscal year (the fiscal year ended March 2025). The company explains that the revenue increase was driven by higher guitar sales, mainly in North America, and higher electronic instrument sales in all regions, although these were partly offset by lower piano sales in China and the end of strong demand for professional audio equipment. Revenue from external customers was ¥304,924 million for musical instruments (up 3.0%), ¥142,444 million for audio equipment (down 3.6%) and ¥17,960 million for other (down 1.4%). The filing states that currency movements increased total revenue by about ¥4.1 billion. Revenue from products and merchandise is recognized when delivered to customers, and revenue from services such as music schools is recognized when the service is provided.

entries.9320b96327832278: This category contains automotive interior components, FA equipment, golf products and the resort business. The securities report states that the reportable segments are 2, "Musical Instruments" and "Audio Equipment," and that other businesses are included in "Others." The businesses in this category are said to make use of the technology and know-how accumulated in the manufacture and sale of musical instruments. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥17,960 million, and business profit was a loss of ¥113 million (a profit of ¥291 million in the previous year). The company explains that demand for automotive interior components and FA equipment was solid and revenue increased, while sales of golf products fell and revenue decreased because of the shrinking of main overseas markets. In February 2026 it announced the end of the golf products business, and ¥1,954 million, including losses on disposal of inventory accompanying this end, was recorded in other expenses as structural reform costs. The number of employees is 818 (consolidated; temporary employees are 214, not included in the figure).
entries.973996e00c8b5eb3: Drawing on YAMAHA CORPORATION’s technical strength and feedback from contracted professional golfers, the company has developed golf clubs that combine function and feel. Entered in 1982, the business has mainly offered golf clubs including the “INPRES” and “RMX” series, but the securities report states that the company decided to end this business in the fiscal year ended March 2026.
entries.984548aec217f80b: This business manufactures and sells sound-related equipment, including home audio equipment, music production and distribution equipment, professional audio equipment, network equipment and mobility audio equipment. According to the securities report, it provides a wide variety of solutions, from consumer products to professional use, by leveraging digital and acoustic technologies developed around sound and music. Manufacturing facilities for professional audio equipment are located at the Toyooka Plant (Iwata City, Shizuoka Prefecture and other locations), and there are also overseas subsidiaries with audio equipment manufacturing facilities, such as Yamaha Electronics Manufacturing (M) Sdn.Bhd. in Malaysia. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥142,444 million, and business profit was ¥10,774 million. For the previous fiscal year (ended March 2025), restated figures were revenue of ¥147,765 million and business profit of ¥14,361 million; revenue fell 3.6% and business profit fell 25.0%. By customer location, revenue is largest in Japan at ¥45,555 million, followed by North America at ¥31,683 million and Europe at ¥30,376 million. The company cites as reasons for the revenue decline that demand for professional audio equipment, which had been high in Europe in the previous fiscal year, has run its course; that it has pursued structural reforms narrowing home audio models and regions; and that sales of mobility audio equipment to Chinese automakers declined. Under the organizational restructuring effective April 1, 2025, the Electronic Devices Division, which manufactured mobility audio equipment and other products, moved into the Audio Business Headquarters, and from this fiscal year, related businesses previously included in 'Other' were transferred to this segment. The number of employees is 4,374 (consolidated; temporary employees are excluded from the total and number 1,268).
entries.a03b92ea28ef40e0: A business that makes and sells musical instruments such as pianos, electronic musical instruments, and wind, string and percussion instruments, and also operates music schools and publishes and distributes sheet music and music; it is the largest of the 3 businesses.
entries.a3b8392792eeb45b: It makes and sells musical instruments, such as pianos and electronic instruments, and audio equipment, such as home audio and professional sound equipment, and earns net sales through its sales companies in Japan and overseas. In addition to musical instruments, it also operates the music school YAMAHA MUSIC SCHOOL in more than 40 countries and regions. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that overseas net sales account for 76.0% of net sales. Regarding order records, it states that "due to the nature of its products, the group basically produces to forecast," meaning it is a business that builds products in advance based on expected sales, rather than producing after receiving orders. Of the net sales of ¥465,330 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026, net sales to external customers were ¥304,924 million for musical instruments, ¥142,444 million for audio equipment, and ¥17,960 million for other businesses, and musical instruments are the largest pillar. Profit is measured as "business profit," which is gross profit minus selling, general and administrative expenses, and profit for each reportable [[term:segment|segment]] is also shown as this business profit.
entries.a747e61d902510c3: Classifying net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 by customer location, Japan was ¥111,771 million, North America ¥124,201 million (of which the United States ¥104,686 million), Europe ¥98,426 million, China ¥43,175 million, and other regions ¥87,754 million, with North America the largest region. Musical instruments are widely used from beginners to professionals, and audio equipment is purchased from consumer products to professional equipment for prominent halls, theaters, concert venues, commercial spaces, and small and medium-sized business sites and stores. Mobility audio equipment is sold to automobile manufacturers, and in the fiscal year ended March 2026, its adoption by Japanese automobile manufacturers expanded, while sales to Chinese automobile manufacturers declined. In Japan, YAMAHA MUSIC JAPAN CO., LTD. purchases and sells the company's products, and overseas, Yamaha Corporation of America in the United States, Yamaha Music Europe GmbH in Germany, and others import and sell them. The securities report also states that there are no external customers whose sales from transactions with a single external customer exceed 10% of net sales.

entries.cbc48f0dc6a84e76: Business profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥31,879 million, a decrease of 13.2% from ¥36,721 million in the previous year. By segment, Musical Instruments recorded ¥21,218 million, Audio Equipment ¥10,774 million, and Other a loss of ¥113 million. The company explains that factors increasing profit, namely currency effects (¥2.7 billion) and the benefit of the previous year's structural reforms (¥2.2 billion), were outweighed by factors reducing profit, namely the net impact of additional US tariffs (¥1.8 billion) and production cuts and model mix, among other factors (¥6.5 billion). After business profit, other income and expenses and finance income and expenses are included: operating profit was ¥29,274 million, profit before tax was ¥35,287 million, and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥23,720 million, an increase of 77.7% from ¥13,351 million in the previous year. Although business profit decreased, other expenses fell by ¥13,055 million (71.4%) from the previous year to ¥5,240 million, and profit before tax rose by ¥12,825 million (57.1%) from the previous year. Other expenses in the previous year included structural reform costs of ¥14,263 million, including impairment losses on piano production facilities and other items. Structural reform costs for the current year were ¥3,336 million, consisting of ¥1,954 million, including inventory disposal losses associated with ending the golf equipment business and other items, and ¥1,381 million of costs related to ending piano production in Indonesia, decided in the previous year.
entries.d14bcb721870df13: The musical instruments business includes acoustic pianos, electronic instruments, hybrid pianos, wind instruments, string instruments, percussion instruments, educational instruments, and soundproof rooms, as well as music schools and English schools, and media and entertainment such as publishing of sheet music, books and magazines, and music distribution. The audio equipment business consists of home audio equipment, music production and distribution equipment, professional sound equipment, network equipment, and mobility audio equipment. "Other" businesses not included in reportable segments include automotive interior components, FA equipment, golf products, and resort business, and in February 2026 it announced the end of its golf products business. Research and development expenses for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥27,720 million (¥12,025 million for musical instruments, ¥14,498 million for audio equipment, and ¥1,197 million for other), with more spent on audio equipment than on musical instruments. In May 2025, the company announced its medium-term management plan "Rebuild & Evolve," and names improving the profitability of the domestic musical instruments business, where profitability has declined for pianos, guitars, and home audio, as its top priority.

entries.ed821d386670afd6: A business that makes and sells musical instruments such as pianos, electronic musical instruments and wind, string and percussion instruments, and also operates music schools and publishes and distributes sheet music and music; it is the largest of the 3 businesses. The securities report explains that it is used by a wide range of people from beginners to professionals, and is supported by research and development carried out in dialogue with artists and by sales and service activities developed worldwide. In Japan, Yamaha Music Japan Co., Ltd. purchases and sells the company's products, and overseas, companies such as Yamaha Corporation of America in the United States and Yamaha Music Europe GmbH in Germany import and sell the company's products. Piano manufacturing facilities are at the Kakegawa Factory (Kakegawa City, Shizuoka Prefecture and elsewhere), and manufacturing facilities for electronic musical instruments and wind, string and percussion instruments are at the Toyooka Factory (Iwata City, Shizuoka Prefecture and elsewhere); there are also manufacturing subsidiaries in China (Tianjin and Hangzhou) and Indonesia. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥304,924 million and business profit (segment profit) was ¥21,218 million. In the previous fiscal year (the fiscal year ended March 2025), revenue was ¥296,100 million and business profit was ¥22,068 million; revenue increased 3.0%, but business profit decreased. The securities report defines business profit as profit equivalent to operating profit under Japanese standards, that is, gross profit less selling, general and administrative expenses. By customer location, revenue is large in North America at ¥84,577 million and Europe at ¥68,045 million, and Japan is ¥58,810 million. The company explains that, although piano sales decreased in China, revenue increased owing to higher guitar sales centered on North America and higher electronic musical instrument sales in all regions. Wind, string and percussion instruments saw solid revenue growth owing to the resumption of wind band activities after the coronavirus pandemic, while pianos saw lower revenue as sales in China, the main market, bottomed out but demand in other markets was also weak. The number of employees is 12,694 (consolidated; temporary employees, not included in this figure, number 4,248).
